To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a novel approach for the extraction of robot parameters that can be used for the simulation of robot dynamics and for the implementation of model-based robot controllers.

we have developed a novel method for the extraction of dynamic parameters from dynamic coefficients, which is able to provide a complete and physically consistent set of dynamic parameters, starting from the linearly parametrized robot dynamics.

the dynamic parameters of a robot can be efficiently extracted from the identified linear dynamic coefficients using global optimization methods, and that the resulting parameters are physically meaningful.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: • Identification of dynamic coefficients from experimental data • Extraction of numerical values of dynamic parameters from identified coefficients • Efficient implementation of model-based controllers on industrial robots • Development of global optimization techniques for nonlinear problems

the following topics: (i) the identification and estimation of the dynamic coefficients of a robot; (ii) the extraction of a complete set of robot dynamic parameters from the identified dynamic coefficients; (iii) the efficient numerical implementation for model-based robot control.
the development of a novel methodology for the identification and extraction of the dynamic parameters of a robot manipulator.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper provides the theoretical basis for a new approach to the dynamic identification of robots.
the proposed methodology is capable of extracting a complete and accurate description of the robot dynamic behavior from dynamic coefficient measurements.

the proposed approach is effective, robust, and computationally efficient, allowing the extraction of all dynamic parameters of a robot arm from the identified values for the linear dynamic coefficients, and providing an accurate estimate of the actual dynamic model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel approach to identify the dynamic model of a robot, and to extract its parameters, using a global nonlinear optimization algorithm.
we have developed a novel methodology to estimate the robot parameters from the linearized dynamic coefficients and validated it on the KUKA LBR IV+ robot.
we can extract the dynamic parameters of a KUKa LWR4 robot from the dynamic coefficients obtained by the system identification process.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by exploiting the physical bounds on the parameters and the global optimization techniques, the proposed approach is able to extract a complete set of feasible parameters that characterize the link dynamics of the considered robot, even when the identification process is affected by measurement noise and modeling errors.
the dynamic parameters can be extracted with a high degree of confidence from the identified dynamic coefficients.
the identification of dynamic coefficients can be a valuable tool for the efficient and accurate numerical implementation of modelbased control algorithms.
